_strings.@@1b01fb3d7bf9: Form 1040N with Nebraska Schedule III (Computation of Nebraska Tax for Nonresidents and Partial-Year Residents); there is no separate nonresident form number — nonresidents and partial-year residents file the same Form 1040N and must attach Schedule III.
_strings.@@1b090f3f0709: Print only the form pages (not instructions), single-sided; attach state copies of W-2/1099.
_strings.@@24bb929482c3: Nebraska Child/Dependent Care Credit (refundable, AGI $29,000 or less) — Full-year and partial-year residents whose federal AGI (Form 1040N, line 5) is $29,000 or less and who have qualifying federal child & dependent care expenses. Must complete and attach Nebraska Form 2441N (the federal Form 2441 alone is not accepted). Taxpayers who file federal MFJ but Nebraska MFS cannot claim it; nonresidents cannot claim it.
_strings.@@2902f3327019: Nebraska Earned Income Credit (state EITC) — Full-year and partial-year Nebraska residents who qualify for and claim the federal Earned Income Credit. Nonresidents may not claim it. If filing Nebraska married-filing-separately, eligibility depends on whether the federal EIC is allowed on a federal MFS return. Paper filers must attach pages 1 and 2 of the federal return.
_strings.@@391542fa43a8: 2024 Nebraska Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form 1040N instructions, 8-307-2024) — What's New (top rate reduced to 5.84% per LB 754; Form PTC community-college-only per LB 34), federal AGI starting point (Line 5), residency definitions, Who Must File, due date, check payee
_strings.@@4cf945d1e9e4: Credit amounts/limits are not independently verified: State credits were researched from the cited DOR sources and are not tax advice — confirm each amount and your eligibility at the cited source before claiming it.
_strings.@@4d42ad525021: Mailing address: Some state facts could not be independently re-confirmed — see the pack's `unverified` list; confirm at the cited DOR source before relying on a specific figure/address.
_strings.@@590a55880908: Nebraska Child/Dependent Care Nonrefundable Credit (AGI over $29,000) — Resident taxpayers with federal AGI greater than $29,000 who claim the federal child & dependent care credit. Must include a copy of federal Form 2441 (credit disallowed if not received). Taxpayers who file federal MFJ but Nebraska MFS cannot claim it; nonresidents may not claim it (partial-year residents use Schedule III line 6c).
_strings.@@76c7f2bac929: 2024 Nebraska Form 1040N (Individual Income Tax Return) — 'Mail returns requesting a refund to: Nebraska Department of Revenue, PO Box 98912, Lincoln NE 68509-8912. Mail returns not requesting a refund to: Nebraska Department of Revenue, PO Box 98934, Lincoln, NE 68509-8934.'
_strings.@@78525e020f7e: Treaty conformity — NE conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from NE income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the NE return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Nebraska's resident return (Form 1040N) starts from federal adjusted gross income: 2024 line 5 is "Federal adjusted gross income (AGI) (line 11, Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR) Do not leave blank." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and therefore flows through. The only additions to federal AGI are on Nebraska Schedule I, Part A ("Adjustments Increasing Federal AGI"), whose nine 2024 line items are: (1) interest income from state/local obligations exempt from federal tax, (2) exempt interest from Nebraska obligations, (3) total taxable interest (line 1 minus line 2), (4) Financial Institution Tax Credit claimed, (5) Nebraska College Savings Program recapture, (6) Nebraska Enable plan recapture, (7) federal net operating loss deduction, (8) S corporation or LLC Non-Nebraska loss, and (9) Nebraska PTET deduction. NONE of these requires adding back income exempt under a U.S. income tax treaty. With no treaty add-back and a federal-AGI starting point, treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed -> Nebraska conforms.
_strings.@@83534fb6c105: Nebraska Personal Exemption Credit (residents only) — Nebraska residents may claim a credit for each Nebraska personal exemption reported on line 4, Form 1040N (taxpayer, spouse, and dependents). Nonresidents and partial-year residents claim a prorated version on Schedule III line 7.
_strings.@@881bd52ef9ba: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): FORM PTC NARROWED TO COMMUNITY COLLEGE PROPERTY TAXES ONLY — for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2024, Form PTC is used ONLY to claim a credit for qualified Nebraska community college property taxes; school district property tax relief is no longer claimed on the income tax return but is applied directly on the property tax statement under the School District Property Tax Relief Act (LB 34, 2024 special session). The 2024 Form PTC Part A line 1 equals the Part B line 2a total with no percentage multiplier. Resolve via: 2024 Nebraska Property Tax Credit, Form PTC and its instructions inside the 2024 Form 1040N booklet (the citation URL), plus the Department's Property Tax Look-up Tool, which computes the qualified community college amounts; school district relief must be read off the property tax statement instead. calc.state_tax applies no Nebraska credits.
_strings.@@b26bb361360b: 2024 Nebraska Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form 1040N instructions, 8-307-2024) — 'Due Date. Your income tax return is due on the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of the tax year (April 15th for calendar-year filers)'; April 15, 2025 for calendar-year 2024 returns
_strings.@@d32bc6575b28: 2024 Nebraska Property Tax Credit, Form PTC instructions (in the 2024 Form 1040N booklet, 8-307-2024) and What's New (Form PTC community-college-only; LB 34 School District Property Tax Relief Act)
_strings.@@d672ebb3d44d: Refund returns: Nebraska Department of Revenue, PO Box 98912, Lincoln, NE 68509-8912. (Note: Nebraska splits addresses by refund vs. no-refund, not refund vs. payment. Returns NOT requesting a refund — including balance-due/with-payment returns — go to PO Box 98934 below.)
_strings.@@e2b82daf5a53: Credit for Community College Property Taxes (Form PTC) — Any individual (and other entities) who paid qualified Nebraska community college property taxes during the 2024 calendar year, directly or through a mortgage escrow. Qualified taxes exclude amounts for bonded indebtedness, voter-approved levy overrides, and property taxes 5+ years delinquent when paid. Must file Form PTC with the return; the DOR Property Tax Look-up Tool computes qualified amounts. NOTE 2024 CHANGE — for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2024, Form PTC is used ONLY for community college property taxes; school district property tax relief is now applied directly on the property tax statement under the School District Property Tax Relief Act (LB 34, 2024 special session), not claimed on the income tax return.

citation.source: 2024 Nebraska Tax Calculation Schedule for Individual Income Tax (8-460-2024), single page — all four filing-status rate tables ("This calculation represents Nebraska income tax before any credits are applied. Enter on line 15, Form 1040N."): Single and Married Filing Separately — 2.46% of Nebraska Taxable Income not over $3,900; $95.94 + 3.51% of the excess over $3,900 to $23,370; $779.34 + 5.01% to $37,670; $1,495.77 + 5.84% over $37,670. Married Filing Jointly and Qualifying Surviving Spouses — 2.46% not over $7,790; $191.63 + 3.51% to $46,760; $1,559.48 + 5.01% to $75,340; $2,991.34 + 5.84% over $75,340. Head of Household — 2.46% not over $7,270; $178.84 + 3.51% to $37,400; $1,236.41 + 5.01% to $55,850; $2,160.75 + 5.84% over $55,850. Standard deduction and line instructions: 2024 Nebraska Individual Income Tax Booklet, Form 1040N (8-307-2024) — What's New ('For the 2024 taxable year, the highest rate for the Nebraska individual income tax is reduced to 5.84%', LB 754, 2023), Line 6 Nebraska Standard Deduction Chart (p.9: Single $8,350 / MFJ $16,700 / QSS $16,700 / MFS $8,350 / HoH $12,250 with zero boxes), Line 15 Nebraska Income Tax and Line 18 personal exemption credit $166 (p.10 area), 2024 Nebraska Tax Table and over-$75,360 worksheet, at https://revenue.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/tax-forms/2024/f_Individual_Income_Tax_Booklet.pdf. Second pass: the standalone 2024 Nebraska Tax Table (https://revenue.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/tax-forms/2024/2024_Tax_Tables.pdf) reproduces the identical math — its $13,060-$13,160 row prints $419/$378/$419/$384, exactly the four schedules at the $13,110 band midpoint, and its over-$75,360 worksheet constants ($3,697 single/MFS, $2,993 MFJ/QSS, $3,300 HoH, each + 5.84% of the excess) equal the schedule evaluated at $75,360 rounded to whole dollars — and the 2024 Form 1040N line 6 prints the same standard deduction amounts. Both passes agree.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 1040N, line 15 "Nebraska income tax" — the 2024 Tax Calculation Schedule states: "This calculation represents Nebraska income tax before any credits are applied. Enter on line 15, Form 1040N." Booklet Line 15 instruction: "Nebraska Income Tax. Nonresidents and partial-year residents, enter the amount from line 9, Nebraska Schedule III. Paper filers may use the Nebraska Tax Table. Electronic filers must use the Nebraska Tax Calculation Schedule." This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2024 CHANGE — TOP RATE CUT TO 5.84% AND BRACKETS RE-INDEXED: the booklet's What's New states 'Individual Income Tax Rate Change (LB 754, 2023). For the 2024 taxable year, the highest rate for the Nebraska individual income tax is reduced to 5.84%' (down from 6.64% in 2023; the lower rates stay 2.46%/3.51%/5.01%). All four schedules' breakpoints are re-indexed for 2024 (Single/MFS $3,900/$23,370/$37,670; MFJ/QSS $7,790/$46,760/$75,340; HoH $7,270/$37,400/$55,850). Do not use 2023 tables or early-2024 withholding-era rates. Base guidance: Supply Form 1040N line 5 — federal adjusted gross income, i.e. Federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11. The pack ships Nebraska's standard deduction for the op to subtract, which reproduces line 14 (Nebraska Taxable Income = line 5 minus line 10 deduction, plus line 12 minus line 13 Schedule I adjustments) whenever there are no Nebraska Schedule I adjustments and the standard deduction is used. If Nebraska Schedule I adjustments apply, supply line 5 plus line 12 minus line 13 instead, so that subtracting the shipped standard deduction still reproduces line 14. Adjudication note (two-pass): vector counts are zero by design — Nebraska personal exemptions are a $166-per-person nonrefundable CREDIT on Form 1040N line 18 for 2024 (raised from $157 in 2023), never an income exemption, so the pack ships no personal/dependent keys and the engine refuses nonzero counts. Nebraska personal exemptions are a TAX CREDIT, not an income exemption: Form 1040N line 18 gives RESIDENTS a nonrefundable credit of $166 times the number of Nebraska personal exemptions on line 4 (yourself, spouse, and dependents; the 2024 form prints '$166 times the number on line 4'). It is subtracted from tax, not from income, so no personal/dependent amounts are shipped in exemptions and calc.state_tax does not apply it — claim it on line 18 of the form (nonresidents and partial-year residents claim it prorated on Nebraska Schedule III, line 7). The shipped standard deduction is the 2024 chart amount with ZERO boxes checked on Form 1040N line 2a (under 65, not blind) for a filer who cannot be claimed for the federal child/dependent tax credit by another taxpayer. Nebraska Standard Deduction Chart (booklet p.9) with line-2a boxes checked: Single $10,300 (1 box) / $12,250 (2); Married Filing Jointly $18,300 / $19,900 / $21,500 / $23,100 (1-4 boxes); Qualifying surviving spouse $18,300 / $19,900 (1-2); Married Filing Separately $9,950 / $11,550 / $13,150 / $14,750 (1-4; the spouse's 65-and-over and blind boxes count only if the primary taxpayer can claim a personal exemption for the spouse); Head of Household $14,200 / $16,150 (1-2). These are NOT applied by calc.state_tax — use the chart amount on line 6. If you or your spouse CAN be claimed by another taxpayer for federal child tax credit or dependent tax credit purposes, your standard deduction is the SMALLER of the federal standard deduction allowed on line 12 of Federal Form 1040/1040-SR or the Nebraska chart amount — not modeled; compute on the form. Itemizers are not modeled: taxpayers who itemized on the federal return take the LARGER of the Nebraska standard deduction or Nebraska itemized deductions (line 9 = federal Schedule A line 17 total minus line 5a state and local income taxes); if you used the federal standard deduction you MUST use the Nebraska standard deduction (booklet p.9, Line 6). Nebraska Schedule I adjustments (Form 1040N line 12 adjustments increasing federal AGI, line 13 adjustments decreasing federal AGI) are not modeled — if they apply, fold them into the supplied base per base_guidance or compute line 14 on the form. Tax table option (paper filers only): 'Only taxpayers filing paper returns may use the Nebraska Tax Table'; electronic filers must use the Tax Calculation Schedule (booklet, Line 15), which is the exact bracket math this op implements. The table calculates tax at the midpoint of each $100 band and covers Nebraska taxable income up to $75,360, so a paper filer's table amount may differ by a few dollars from this op's result within a band; above $75,360 the booklet worksheet is (taxable income - $75,360) x .0584 plus $3,697 Single/MFS, $2,993 MFJ/QSS, or $3,300 HoH. Qualifying surviving spouse: the schedule's second table is titled 'Married Taxpayers, Filing Jointly and Qualifying Surviving Spouses' — the engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping is exact for the brackets, and the QSS standard deduction with zero boxes is the same $16,700. Married filing separately is printed with the SAME schedule as Single on the 2024 Tax Calculation Schedule (identical breakpoints $3,900/$23,370/$37,670 and constants) — copied from the MFS table, not derived. The schedule's printed '$X + Y% of excess over $Z' constants are the exact cumulative bracket sums rounded to the nearest cent; maximum divergence from the exact sum is $0.005 (Single/MFS $779.34 vs exact $779.337 and $1,495.77 vs $1,495.767; MFJ $191.63 vs $191.634, $1,559.48 vs $1,559.481, $2,991.34 vs $2,991.339; HoH $178.84 vs $178.842, $1,236.41 vs $1,236.405; the HoH top constant $2,160.75 is exact) — after rounding to whole dollars the results agree. Nebraska other tax is NOT modeled: Form 1040N line 16 adds 29.6% (x .296) of federal tax on lump-sum distributions of qualified retirement plans (Federal Form 4972) and federal tax on early distributions (lesser of Federal Form 5329 or Schedule 2 line 8); line 17 total tax = line 15 + line 16. Nonresidents and partial-year residents are NOT modeled: they compute line 15 via Nebraska Schedule III (line 9), which apportions the tax by the Nebraska-income ratio. Standard deduction chart source: 2024 Nebraska Individual Income Tax Booklet (8-307-2024), Line 6, p.9 — https://revenue.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/tax-forms/2024/f_Individual_Income_Tax_Booklet.pdf
